title.narrative: Provision of integrated, life-saving Nutrition and Protection assistance to the most severely drought affected families in Hargeisa

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSave the Children (SC) proposes a lifesaving nutrition and protection intervention targeting drought-affected rural communities in Hargeisa district, where persistent food insecurity, limited access to basic services, and rising malnutrition rates continue to place children and pregnant and lactating women at high risk. The project aims to increase equitable access to quality, lifesaving curative and preventive nutrition services while strengthening community-based protection systems, positive caregiving practices, and safe referral pathways. The project will operate across 10 nutrition service delivery points, including eight fixed facilities—Bali-Mataan HC, ltbrgtXunboweyne MCH, Bali-Cabane MCH, Gumar HF, Dacarta MCH, Dhimbil-Riyaale MCH, Sayla Bari MCH, and Bandar Wanaag—and two mobile outreach locations, Qoolbulale HC and Higlada MCH, which are served through one mobile nutrition team and their surrounding catchment areas. Through this model, SC will deliver integrated community and facility-based services for screening, early detection, treatment of SAM, referrals, IYCF counselling, micronutrient supplementation, and protection awareness.ltbrgtSC will support Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) services for the treatment of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) according to Somalia IMAM guidelines. Children identified with MUAC lt11gtCommunity-based screening, mobilization, and protection risk identification will be led by 28 trained Community Nutrition Volunteers and Community Health Promoters, supported by 14 IYCF counsellors. SC will reinforce community capacities through structured awareness sessions on harmful practices, child protection risks, and safe reporting, reaching 1828 caregivers. Referral pathways for child protection, nutrition, and GBV will be strengthened through updated service mapping and dissemination to frontline workers and community structures.To ensure accountability, SC will operationalize inclusive Feedback and Response Mechanisms including hotline 3061, suggestion boxes, community feedback sessions, and FGDs—across all 10 supported nutrition sites. These mechanisms will promote safe, confidential reporting and strengthen community engagement in service improvement.ltbrgtThrough trained and qualified staff, the project will reach 27,714 crisis-affected individuals (Women: 9,620, Girls: 10,273, Men: 748, Boys: 7073) with lifesaving SAM treatment, preventive nutrition services, IYCF support, community-based screening, and strengthened child protection systems across rural areas in Hargeisa district.ltbrgtlt/pgt
